SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - OCTOBER 9, 2017 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
OCTOBER 9, 2017, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Paul Hansen, First Christian Reformed
  Church, Artesia.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was given by City of Cerritos Recreation Services
  Division Rookie III Flag Football Team, “Cowboys.”

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations were presented to:

  Friends of the Cerritos Library (National Friends of Libraries Week).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Mel Cortez expressed support for the growth of the Neighborhood Watch program
  and noted the decrease in home break-ins over the last few weeks. He requested
  assistance from the Community Safety Division for copying Neighborhood Watch
  meeting flyers. He inquired whether the City could send out an automatic
  response email when residents email the City.

  Judi Erikson requested the City continue to allow residents to utilize the pool for
  casual water aerobics gatherings.

  Paula Gamble requested the City continue to allow residents to utilize the pool for
  casual water aerobics gatherings.

  Sandy Fikse requested the City continue to allow residents to utilize the pool for
  casual water aerobics gatherings.

  Barbara Durstan requested the City continue to allow residents to utilize the pool
  for casual water aerobics gatherings.

  Julie Craig requested the City continue to allow residents to utilize the pool for
  casual water aerobics gatherings.
 City of Cerritos  October 9, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 6

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Jay Gray requested that Consent Calendar Item No. 7A be removed from
  consideration from tonight’s meeting as the minutes were not posted to the City’s
  website.

  Sam Desai spoke regarding his website, OurCerritos.org, and additional
  information provided on their Facebook page. He also referenced the upcoming
  ABC Unified School District election and the potential of new taxes.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  September 28, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of September 28, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Registers of Demands

  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated October 9, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the
  Registers of Demands as follows:

  1. City of Cerritos  10/09/2017 $7,037,078.62 (COUNCIL)
  2. Successor Agency  10/09/2017 $13,846,340.00 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  October 9, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 6

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council Treasurer’s Report for the period ending August 31,
  2017 (COUNCIL).

  Approval of the Successor Agency’s Treasurer’s Report for the period ending August
  31, 2017 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to approve the
  Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending August 31, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Award of contract for the printing of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts
  2017-2018 calendar of events, Bid No. 1318-17 (COUNCIL).

  This item was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to award Bid No.
  1318-17 for the printing of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts 2017-2018
  Calendar of Events to Trend Offset Printing in the amount of $60,962.83. In the
  event issues of non-performance arise, the project would be removed from Trend
  Offset Printing and taken to the next lowest bidder to ensure the City’s printing
  deadline, quality standards, and specifications are met. This process would be
  repeated as necessary in order of the lowest bid to the highest (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7E.  Award of a contract for Swim Center extraordinary maintenance, RFB No. 1320-17
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to award a contract
  for Annual Swim Center extraordinary maintenance to Service 1st Contractors.

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.
 City of Cerritos  October 9, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 6

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of approval of a maintenance service contract for the
  existing Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system for the City of
  Cerritos Water Department (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Senior Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Pulido, to:

  1. Award the maintenance service support contract to HSQ Technologies in the
  amount of $1,300.00 per month. The service contract may be extended
  administratively for one additional year, upon concurrence by both parties; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of expenditures of grant funds for the improvements to the
  City-owned property located at 18616 Bloomfield Avenue (APN 7030-002-903)
  adjacent to Heritage Park and the renovation of the Cerritos Sports Complex athletic
  fields (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sherre Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to:

  1. Direct the City Manager to proceed with the bid process related to the site
  improvements of the City-owned property located at 18616 Bloomfield Avenue;
  and
  2. Direct staff to continue to work with a consultant to determine a remedy to
  improve the condition of the athletic fields at the Cerritos Sports Complex and
  prepare a timeline for renovation of the recommended fields; and
  3. Direct the City Manager to proceed with the bid process related to the
  renovation of the athletic fields at the Cerritos Sports Complex (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  October 9, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  Review and consideration of award of contract for Cerritos Senior Center carpentry
  maintenance, Bid No. 1317-17 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaren, Director of Public Works. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $154,000.00 for Senior Center Exterior
  Improvements (total bid), Bid No. 1317-17, to RS Construction Services and reject
  the other bid; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for Cerritos Parkway Tree
  maintenance, RFB No. 1310-17 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Scott P. Griffiths, owner of Great Scott Tree Service, introduced his company and
  responded to inquiries from the City Council.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $554,795.00 for Cerritos Parkway Tree
  Maintenance, RFB No. 1310-17, to Great Scott Tree Service and reject all other bids.
  This includes $350,00.00 toward Bid Item No. 1 for tree trimming and $204,795.00
  for Bid Item No. 3 for residential tree removals; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders, which may include additional trimming in the current fiscal year
  and an additional grid trimming project in the amount of $735,000.00 should
  the City Council allocate funding for tree trimming in the 2018-19 fiscal year
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  October 9, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 6

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal Legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Yokoyama, Solanki, and Edwards,
  Mayor Pro Tem Pulido, and Mayor Hu.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned at 10:09 p.m.
